**_Abstract_**

**SoleMates: Love at First Step** is an innovative and dynamic online shoe store designed to deliver a seamless shopping experience for fashion-forward customers. This platform transforms the way users explore and purchase footwear by integrating modern technologies with user-friendly design. SoleMates provides an interactive and responsive interface where users can browse a diverse range of products, apply filters, view detailed product descriptions, and enjoy personalized shopping features like wishlists, search functionality, and dynamic cart management.

Our website supports two primary user roles: Store Users and Administrators. Store Users can create accounts, browse through men's and women's collections, add items to their cart, and proceed through a streamlined checkout process with real-time stock validation. Administrators, on the other hand, gain full control of the system, managing products, inventory, and users via a secure backend.

Built using **Django** for the web framework and **Microsoft SQL Server** for robust database management, SoleMates integrates core DBMS concepts such as stored procedures, triggers, and dynamic SQL schema generation via Django's ORM models. Security and data integrity are ensured with features like audit trails for product, order, and stock changes, and stock validation triggers prevent over-purchasing.

This project not only revamps an earlier prototype into a full-fledged e-commerce solution but also encapsulates advanced concepts in database management and web development. With a modern, engaging interface and a tagline that captures its spirit-"Love at First Step!"-SoleMates is set to redefine the digital shoe shopping experience.

# Introduction

**SoleMates is not just a shoe store - it's your digital runway for finding the perfect pair!**  
Our website blends style, convenience, and technology, offering customers an immersive platform to browse, select, and order premium shoes. Whether you're looking for men's classics or women's statement heels, SoleMates makes it simple to **step into style** with just a few clicks.

Behind the scenes, SoleMates is powered by a **dynamic database** that manages product listings, user profiles, orders, and real-time stock updates. The platform features intuitive navigation, secure authentication, and seamless order tracking, giving users a complete shopping experience.

This project **elevates our previous prototype** by transforming a static, two-page website into a fully interactive, database-driven e-commerce platform. It's not just a revamp - it's a complete reimagination of what online shoe shopping can be!

# Problem Statement

Shoe shopping online can be frustrating with outdated websites, unreliable inventory updates, and clunky user experiences. Our original site was basic and couldn't deliver the dynamic shopping experience customers expect. It lacked real-time stock tracking, user accounts, and the ability to handle orders or manage data effectively. SoleMates needed an upgrade to become a **trendy, seamless, and data-driven shoe store that meets modern e-commerce standards**.

# Proposed Solution

SoleMates now offers a **walk-in closet of features**, ensuring every step of the customer journey is smooth and stylish. From **signing up and browsing collections** to **adding favorites to your cart and checking out**, everything is handled dynamically with robust database support.

## Features of the project

- **User Authentication & Profiles:** Users can register, log in, and view their personal order history.
- **Dynamic Product Catalog:** Explore curated men's and women's collections, filter by category, and view detailed product pages.
- **Interactive Cart & Checkout:** Add items to your cart with real-time stock validation. Enjoy a smooth checkout with auto-filled billing details and secure order placement.
- **Admin Dashboard:** Superusers can access Django's admin interface to manage products, stock levels, and view detailed database tables.
- **Search & Discover:** Use the search bar to find your next pair and view suggestions for related styles.
- **Audit Logging & Integrity:** Advanced triggers and stored procedures maintain data consistency and track key actions.
- **E-Bill Generation:** Get a digital bill after checkout - print it or go paperless.

## Methodology

We combined the power of **Django's web framework** with **Microsoft SQL Server** to manage data efficiently. Through **iterative development**, we built features step-by-step, integrating raw SQL for complex database operations, and used AJAX to make cart updates smooth and interactive. Our approach ensured that both functionality and user experience were at the forefront.

## Technologies

- **Backend:** Django (Python), Django ORM, Raw SQL, Microsoft SQL Server
- **Frontend:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript, AJAX
- **Database:** SQL Server for robust data management
- **Version Control:** Git for tracking progress

# Software Design Description

## Design Overview

SoleMates is built on a **Model-View-Template (MVT)** architecture that ensures efficient handling of data and smooth rendering of content. Models define the structure of products, users, and orders. Views handle logic and interactions, while templates present the data attractively to users.

from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError

class CartItem(models.Model):

&nbsp; cart = models.ForeignKey(Cart, related_name='items', on_delete=models.CASCADE)

&nbsp; product = models.ForeignKey(Product, on_delete=models.CASCADE)

&nbsp; quantity = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=1)

&nbsp; @property

&nbsp; def total_price(self):

&nbsp; return self.product.price \* self.quantity

&nbsp; def clean(self):

&nbsp; stock = Stock.objects.filter(product=self.product).first()

&nbsp; if stock and self.quantity > stock.quantity:

&nbsp; raise ValidationError(f"Cannot add more than {stock.quantity} items of this product to the cart.")

&nbsp; def save(self, \*args, \*\*kwargs):

&nbsp; self.clean()

&nbsp; super().save(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

\# AUTH USER RELATED

from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractBaseUser, PermissionsMixin, BaseUserManager

from django.db import models

class StoreUserManager(BaseUserManager):

&nbsp; def create_user(self, username, email, password=None, \*\*extra_fields):

&nbsp; if not email:

&nbsp; raise ValueError('Email is required')

&nbsp; email = self.normalize_email(email)

&nbsp; user = self.model(username=username, email=email, \*\*extra_fields)

&nbsp; user.set_password(password)

&nbsp; user.save(using=self.\_db)

&nbsp; return user

&nbsp; def create_superuser(self, username, email, password=None, \*\*extra_fields):

&nbsp; extra_fields.setdefault('is_staff', True)

&nbsp; extra_fields.setdefault('is_superuser', True)

&nbsp; return self.create_user(username, email, password, \*\*extra_fields)

class StoreUser(AbstractBaseUser, PermissionsMixin):

&nbsp; username = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True)

&nbsp; email = models.EmailField(unique=True)

&nbsp; first_name = models.CharField(max_length=100, null=True, blank=True)

&nbsp; last_name = models.CharField(max_length=100, null=True, blank=True)

&nbsp; is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)

&nbsp; is_staff = models.BooleanField(default=False)

&nbsp; date_joined = models.DateTimeField(default=timezone.now)

&nbsp; USERNAME_FIELD = 'username'

&nbsp; REQUIRED_FIELDS = \['email'\]

&nbsp; objects = StoreUserManager()

&nbsp; def \__str_\_(self):

&nbsp; return self.username

&nbsp;

@login_required

def add_to_cart(request):

&nbsp; if request.method == 'POST':

&nbsp; product_ids = request.POST.getlist('product_ids')

&nbsp; if not product_ids:

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "Please select at least one product")

&nbsp; return redirect('women')

&nbsp; user_id = request.user.id

&nbsp; with connection.cursor() as cursor:

&nbsp; # Get or create customer

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT id FROM store_customer WHERE user_id = %s", \[user_id\])

&nbsp; customer_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if customer_row:

&nbsp; customer_id = customer_row\[0\]

&nbsp; else:

&nbsp; cursor.execute(

&nbsp; "INSERT INTO store_customer (user_id) OUTPUT INSERTED.id VALUES (%s)", \[user_id\]

&nbsp; )

&nbsp; customer_id = cursor.fetchone()\[0\]

&nbsp; # Get or create cart

&nbsp; cursor.execute(

&nbsp; "SELECT id FROM store_cart WHERE customer_id = %s AND is_active = 1", \[customer_id\]

&nbsp; )

&nbsp; cart_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if cart_row:

&nbsp; cart_id = cart_row\[0\]

&nbsp; else:

&nbsp; cursor.execute(

&nbsp; "INSERT INTO store_cart (customer_id, is_active, created_at, updated_at) "

&nbsp; "OUTPUT INSERTED.id VALUES (%s, 1, %s, %s)",

&nbsp; \[customer_id, timezone.now(), timezone.now()\]

@login_required

def update_cart(request):

&nbsp; if request.method == 'POST':

&nbsp; item_id = request.POST.get('item_id')

&nbsp; quantity = request.POST.get('quantity')

&nbsp; user_id = request.user.id

&nbsp; with connection.cursor() as cursor:

&nbsp; # Verify cart item belongs to user

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; SELECT ci.id, c.id

&nbsp; FROM store_cartitem ci

&nbsp; JOIN store_cart c ON ci.cart_id = c.id

&nbsp; JOIN store_customer cust ON c.customer_id = cust.id

&nbsp; WHERE ci.id = %s AND cust.user_id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[item_id, user_id\])

&nbsp; item = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if item:

&nbsp; cursor.execute("UPDATE store_cartitem SET quantity = %s WHERE id = %s", \[quantity, item_id\])

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; SELECT SUM(p.price \* ci.quantity)

&nbsp; FROM store_cartitem ci

&nbsp; JOIN store_product p ON ci.product_id = p.id

&nbsp; WHERE ci.cart_id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[item\[1\]\])

&nbsp; subtotal = cursor.fetchone()\[0\] or 0

&nbsp; total = subtotal # Add tax/delivery/discount if needed

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; SELECT (p.price \* ci.quantity)

&nbsp; FROM store_cartitem ci

&nbsp; JOIN store_product p ON ci.product_id = p.id

&nbsp; WHERE ci.id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[item_id\])

&nbsp; item_total = cursor.fetchone()\[0\] or 0

&nbsp; return JsonResponse({

&nbsp; 'item_total': f"{item_total:.2f}",

&nbsp; 'subtotal': f"{subtotal:.2f}",

&nbsp; 'total': f"{total:.2f}"

&nbsp; })

&nbsp; else:

&nbsp; return JsonResponse({'error': 'Cart item not found'}, status=404)

&nbsp; return JsonResponse({'error': 'Invalid request'}, status=400)

@login_required

def place_order(request):

&nbsp; if request.method != 'POST':

&nbsp; print("Request method is not POST, redirecting to checkout")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; required_fields = \[\]

&nbsp; for field in required_fields:

&nbsp; if not request.POST.get(field):

&nbsp; print(f"Missing required field in POST data: {field}")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, f"Missing required field: {field}")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; try:

&nbsp; with transaction.atomic():

&nbsp; user_id = request.user.id

&nbsp; print(f"User ID: {user_id}")

&nbsp; with connection.cursor() as cursor:

&nbsp; print("Inserting billing details...")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; INSERT INTO store_billingdetails

&nbsp; (user_id, country, first_name, last_name, company_name, address, address2, city, state, zip_code, email, phone, payment_method, created_at)

&nbsp; VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, GETDATE())

&nbsp; """, \[

&nbsp; user_id,

&nbsp; request.POST.get('country', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('fname', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('lname', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('companyname', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('address', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('address2', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('towncity', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('stateprovince', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('zippostalcode', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('email', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('phone', ''),

&nbsp; request.POST.get('payment_method', ''),

&nbsp; \])

&nbsp; print("Billing details inserted.")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT TOP 1 id FROM store_billingdetails WHERE user_id = %s ORDER BY created_at DESC", \[user_id\])

&nbsp; billing_id_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if not billing_id_row:

&nbsp; print("Failed to retrieve billing details ID.")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "Failed to create billing details.")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; billing_id = billing_id_row\[0\]

&nbsp; print(f"Billing ID: {billing_id}")

&nbsp; customer = Customer.objects.filter(user=request.user).first()

&nbsp; if not customer:

&nbsp; print("Customer not found for user.")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "Customer not found.")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; customer_id = customer.id

&nbsp; print(f"Customer ID: {customer_id}")

&nbsp; with connection.cursor() as cursor:

&nbsp; print("Fetching active cart ID...")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT TOP 1 id FROM store_cart WHERE customer_id = %s AND is_active = 1", \[customer_id\])

&nbsp; cart_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if not cart_row:

&nbsp; print("No active cart found for customer.")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "No active cart found.")

&nbsp; return redirect('cart')

&nbsp; cart_id = cart_row\[0\]

&nbsp; print(f"Cart ID: {cart_id}")

&nbsp; print("Fetching cart items...")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; SELECT ci.id, ci.product_id, ci.quantity

&nbsp; FROM store_cartitem ci

&nbsp; WHERE ci.cart_id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[cart_id\])

&nbsp; cart_items = cursor.fetchall()

&nbsp; print(f"Number of cart items: {len(cart_items)}")

&nbsp; if not cart_items:

&nbsp; print("Cart is empty.")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "Your cart is empty.")

&nbsp; return redirect('cart')

&nbsp; print("Inserting order...")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; INSERT INTO store_order (customer_id, billing_details_id, total, complete, date_ordered)

&nbsp; VALUES (%s, %s, 0, 0, GETDATE())

&nbsp; """, \[customer_id, billing_id\])

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT TOP 1 id FROM store_order WHERE customer_id = %s ORDER BY date_ordered DESC", \[customer_id\])

&nbsp; order_id_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if not order_id_row:

&nbsp; print("Failed to create order.")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, "Failed to create order.")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; order_id = order_id_row\[0\] # This is the raw order ID from SQL

&nbsp; print(f"Order ID: {order_id}")

&nbsp; total_amount = 0

&nbsp; for item in cart_items:

&nbsp; cartitem_id, product_id, quantity = item

&nbsp; print(f"Processing cart item - Product ID: {product_id}, Quantity: {quantity}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT price FROM store_product WHERE id = %s", \[product_id\])

&nbsp; price_row = cursor.fetchone()

&nbsp; if not price_row:

&nbsp; print(f"Product not found with ID {product_id}")

&nbsp; messages.error(request, f"Product with ID {product_id} not found.")

&nbsp; return redirect('cart')

&nbsp; price = price_row\[0\]

&nbsp; item_total = price \* quantity

&nbsp; total_amount += item_total

&nbsp; print(f"Item total: {item_total}, Running total: {total_amount}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; INSERT INTO store_orderitem (order_id, product_id, quantity,date_added)

&nbsp; VALUES (%s, %s, %s,%s)

&nbsp; """, \[order_id, product_id, quantity,timezone.now()\])

&nbsp; print(f"Inserted order item for product {product_id}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; UPDATE store_stock SET quantity = quantity - %s WHERE product_id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[quantity, product_id\])

&nbsp; print(f"Updated stock for product {product_id}")

&nbsp; print(f"Updating order total to: {total_amount}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; UPDATE store_order SET total = %s WHERE id = %s

&nbsp; """, \[total_amount, order_id\])

&nbsp; print(f"Deactivating cart ID: {cart_id}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("UPDATE store_cart SET is_active = 0 WHERE id = %s", \[cart_id\])

&nbsp; print(f"Deleting cart items for cart ID: {cart_id}")

&nbsp; cursor.execute("DELETE FROM store_cartitem WHERE cart_id = %s", \[cart_id\])

&nbsp; messages.success(request, "Your order has been placed successfully!")

&nbsp; print("Order placed successfully, redirecting to order_complete.")

&nbsp; # Use the order_id we got from the SQL query, not order.id

&nbsp; print(f"Created order with ID: {order_id}")

&nbsp; return redirect('order_complete', order_id=order_id) # Fixed this line

&nbsp; except Exception as e:

&nbsp; import traceback

&nbsp; traceback.print_exc() # Full traceback in console/log

&nbsp; messages.error(request, f"Error placing order: {str(e)}")

&nbsp; print(f"Exception caught in place_order: {e}")

&nbsp; return redirect('checkout')

&nbsp; sql += " AND brand = %s"

&nbsp; params.append(brand)

&nbsp; sql += " AND technologies LIKE %s"

&nbsp; # Execute raw SQL query

def register(request):

&nbsp; if request.method == 'POST':

&nbsp; username = request.POST\['username'\]

&nbsp; email = request.POST\['email'\]

&nbsp; password = request.POST\['password1'\]

&nbsp; password_confirm = request.POST\['password2'\]

&nbsp; if password != password_confirm:

&nbsp; return render(request, 'registration/register.html', {'error': 'Passwords do not match'})

&nbsp; with connection.cursor() as cursor:

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT id FROM store_storeuser WHERE username = %s", \[username\])

&nbsp; if cursor.fetchone():

&nbsp; return render(request, 'registration/register.html', {'error': 'Username already exists'})

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT id FROM store_storeuser WHERE email = %s", \[email\])

&nbsp; if cursor.fetchone():

&nbsp; return render(request, 'registration/register.html', {'error': 'Email already exists'})

&nbsp; hashed_password = make_password(password)

&nbsp; cursor.execute("""

&nbsp; INSERT INTO store_storeuser (username, password, email, is_active, is_staff, is_superuser, date_joined)

&nbsp; VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, GETDATE())

&nbsp; """, \[username, hashed_password, email, True, False, False\])

&nbsp; # Get the new user's ID

&nbsp; cursor.execute("SELECT id FROM store_storeuser WHERE username = %s", \[username\])

&nbsp; user_id = cursor.fetchone()\[0\]

&nbsp; user = get_user_by_id(user_id)

&nbsp; login(request, user)

&nbsp; return redirect('home')

&nbsp; return render(request, 'registration/register.html')

def user_login(request):

&nbsp; if request.method == 'POST':

&nbsp; username = request.POST\['username'\]

&nbsp; password = request.POST\['password'\]

&nbsp; user = get_user_by_username(username)

&nbsp; if user and check_password(password, user.password):

&nbsp; login(request, user)

&nbsp; # Redirect based on whether user is superuser

&nbsp; if user.is_superuser:

&nbsp; return redirect('/admin/') # Django admin panel

&nbsp; else:

&nbsp; return redirect('home') # Normal user home page

&nbsp; else:

def update_profile(request):

def search_view(request):

def product_detail(request):

&nbsp; product_id = request.GET.get('product_id')

&nbsp; if not product_id:

&nbsp; return HttpResponseNotFound("Product ID not provided")

&nbsp; product = get_object_or_404(Product, id=product_id)

&nbsp;

&nbsp; related_products = RelatedProducts.objects.filter(

&nbsp; base_product_id=product_id

&nbsp; ).order_by('-similarity_score')\[:4\]

&nbsp;

&nbsp; related_product_objects = Product.objects.filter(

&nbsp; id_\_in=\[rp.related_product_id for rp in related_products\]

&nbsp; )

&nbsp; context = {

&nbsp; 'product': product,

&nbsp; 'sizes': product.get_available_sizes(),

&nbsp; 'widths': product.get_available_widths(),

&nbsp; 'related_products': related_product_objects

&nbsp; }

&nbsp; return render(request, 'product-detail.html', context)

**DJANGO ORM TO SCHEMA:**

CREATE DATABASE \[SoleMatesDB\]

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_product (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

name nvarchar(200) NOT NULL,

brand nvarchar(10) NULL,

material nvarchar(10) NULL,

price numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (price >= 0),

gender nvarchar(1) NOT NULL,

style nvarchar(3) NOT NULL,

sizes nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

width nvarchar(1) NOT NULL,

colors nvarchar(200) NOT NULL,

technologies nvarchar(200) NOT NULL,

purchase_count int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (purchase_count >= 0),

image nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

created_at datetimeoffset NOT NULL

)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_user (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

username nvarchar(150) NOT NULL UNIQUE,

password nvarchar(128) NOT NULL,

email nvarchar(254) NOT NULL,

first_name nvarchar(150) NOT NULL,

last_name nvarchar(150) NOT NULL,

phone nvarchar(20) NOT NULL,

address nvarchar(max) NOT NULL,

is_active bit NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

is_customer bit NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

date_joined datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

last_login datetimeoffset NULL

)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_customer (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

user_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_user(id),

phone nvarchar(20) NULL,

address nvarchar(255) NULL

)

CREATE INDEX idx_customer_user ON store_customer(user_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_stock (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

product_id bigint NOT NULL UNIQUE FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_product(id),

quantity int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (quantity >= 0),

last_updated datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET()

)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_cart (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

customer_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_customer(id),

created_at datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

updated_at datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

is_active bit NOT NULL DEFAULT 1

)

CREATE INDEX idx_cart_customer ON store_cart(customer_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_cartitem (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

cart_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_cart(id),

product_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_product(id),

quantity int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (quantity >= 0)

)

CREATE INDEX idx_cartitem_cart ON store_cartitem(cart_id)

CREATE INDEX idx_cartitem_product ON store_cartitem(product_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_billingdetails (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

user_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_user(id),

first_name nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

last_name nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

email nvarchar(254) NOT NULL,

phone nvarchar(20) NOT NULL,

address nvarchar(255) NOT NULL,

city nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

state nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

zip_code nvarchar(20) NOT NULL,

country nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,

payment_method nvarchar(50) NOT NULL,

created_at datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET()

)

CREATE INDEX idx_billing_user ON store_billingdetails(user_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_order (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

customer_id bigint NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_customer(id),

billing_details_id bigint NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_billingdetails(id),

date_ordered datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

total numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (total >= 0),

complete bit NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

transaction_id nvarchar(100) NULL

)

CREATE INDEX idx_order_customer ON store_order(customer_id)

CREATE INDEX idx_order_billing ON store_order(billing_details_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.store_orderitem (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

order_id bigint NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_order(id),

product_id bigint NULL FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES store_product(id),

quantity int NOT NULL CHECK (quantity >= 0),

date_added datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET()

)

CREATE INDEX idx_orderitem_order ON store_orderitem(order_id)

CREATE INDEX idx_orderitem_product ON store_orderitem(product_id)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.stock_audit (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

action_time datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

action_type nvarchar(10) NOT NULL,

stock_id int NOT NULL,

product_id int NULL,

quantity_before int NULL,

quantity_after int NULL

)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.product_audit (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

action_time datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

action_type nvarchar(10) NOT NULL,

product_id int NOT NULL,

product_name nvarchar(255) NULL,

stock_before int NULL,

stock_after int NULL

)

GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.order_audit (

id bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,

action_time datetimeoffset NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET(),

action_type nvarchar(10) NOT NULL,

order_id int NOT NULL,

customer_id int NULL,

total numeric(10, 2) NULL

)

GO

**VIEWS:**

\-- 1. best_sellers_view

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW best_sellers_view AS

SELECT

p.id AS product_id,

p.name AS product_name,

p.price AS product_price,

p.image AS product_image_url,

SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_purchases

FROM

store_orderitem oi

JOIN

store_product p ON oi.product_id = p.id

GROUP BY

p.id, p.name, p.price, p.image;

\-- 2. user_profile_view

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW user_profile_view AS

SELECT

u.id AS user_id,

u.username,

u.first_name,

u.last_name,

u.email,

p.image as product_image_url,

c.id AS customer_id,

p.id AS product_id,

p.name AS product_name,

p.price AS product_price,

o.date_ordered

FROM

store_user u

JOIN

store_customer c ON c.user_id = u.id

LEFT JOIN

store_order o ON o.customer_id = c.id

LEFT JOIN

store_orderitem oi ON oi.order_id = o.id

LEFT JOIN

store_product p ON p.id = oi.product_id;

\-- 3. search_products_view

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW search_products_view AS

SELECT

id,

name,

price,

brand,

material,

gender,

style,

sizes,

colors,

technologies,

image

FROM store_product;

\-- 4. related_products_view

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW related_products_view AS

SELECT

p1.id AS base_product_id,

p2.id AS related_product_id,

p2.name,

p2.brand,

p2.price,

p2.image,

p2.gender,

p2.style,

(

\-- Brand match (most important)

CASE WHEN p1.brand = p2.brand THEN 4 ELSE 0 END +

\-- Style match

CASE WHEN p1.style = p2.style THEN 3 ELSE 0 END +

\-- Gender match

CASE WHEN p1.gender = p2.gender THEN 2 ELSE 0 END +

\-- Price within 30% range

CASE WHEN p2.price BETWEEN p1.price \* 0.7 AND p1.price \* 1.3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +

\-- Material match

CASE WHEN p1.material = p2.material THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

) AS similarity_score,

p2.material,

p2.colors

FROM

store_product p1

JOIN

store_product p2 ON p1.id != p2.id

WHERE

(p1.brand = p2.brand OR

p1.style = p2.style OR

p1.gender = p2.gender OR

p1.material = p2.material OR

p2.price BETWEEN p1.price \* 0.7 AND p1.price \* 1.3);

\-- 5. new_arrivals

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW new_arrivals AS

SELECT

id,

name,

price,

image as product_image_url,

created_at

FROM store_product

WHERE created_at >= DATEADD(day, -30, GETDATE());

**TRIGGERS:**

\--TRIGGERS:

\--AUDIT TRIGGER:

\--FOR PRODUCT:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_audit_store_product

ON store_product

AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

AS

BEGIN

SET NOCOUNT ON;

\-- INSERT: When a product is added

INSERT INTO product_audit (

action_time, action_type, product_id, product_name, stock_before, stock_after

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'INSERT',

i.id,

i.name,

COALESCE(s.quantity, 0) AS stock_before, -- Default to 0 if no stock yet

COALESCE(s.quantity, 0) AS stock_after

FROM inserted i

LEFT JOIN store_stock s ON i.id = s.product_id;

\-- DELETE: When a product is deleted

INSERT INTO product_audit (

action_time, action_type, product_id, product_name, quantity, amount_paid, stock_before, stock_after

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'DELETE',

d.id,

d.name,

oi.quantity,

(oi.quantity \* p.price), -- Approximate amount_paid = quantity \* price

s.quantity,

NULL

FROM deleted d

LEFT JOIN store_stock s ON d.id = s.product_id

LEFT JOIN store_orderitem oi ON d.id = oi.product_id

LEFT JOIN store_product p ON d.id = p.id;

\-- UPDATE: When a product is updated

INSERT INTO product_audit (

action_time, action_type, product_id, product_name, quantity, amount_paid, stock_before, stock_after

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'UPDATE',

i.id,

i.name,

oi.quantity,

(oi.quantity \* p.price),

s.quantity,

s.quantity -- You could optionally calculate before/after by keeping track of changes in stock table

FROM inserted i

INNER JOIN deleted d ON i.id = d.id

LEFT JOIN store_stock s ON i.id = s.product_id

LEFT JOIN store_orderitem oi ON i.id = oi.product_id

LEFT JOIN store_product p ON i.id = p.id;

END;

\--FOR STOCK:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_audit_store_stock

ON store_stock

AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

AS

BEGIN

SET NOCOUNT ON;

\-- INSERT: Pull product name from store_product table

INSERT INTO stock_audit (

action_time, action_type, stock_id, product_id, quantity_before, quantity_after, last_updated, product_name

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'INSERT',

i.id,

i.product_id,

0, -- Before insert, assume quantity was 0

i.quantity,

i.last_updated,

p.name -- Get product name from store_product

FROM inserted i

LEFT JOIN store_product p ON i.product_id = p.id;

\-- DELETE: Capture stock and product info

INSERT INTO stock_audit (

action_time, action_type, stock_id, product_id, quantity_before, quantity_after, last_updated, product_name

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'DELETE',

d.id,

d.product_id,

d.quantity,

NULL,

d.last_updated,

p.name

FROM deleted d

LEFT JOIN store_product p ON d.product_id = p.id;

\-- UPDATE: Show before and after quantities, with product name

INSERT INTO stock_audit (

action_time, action_type, stock_id, product_id, quantity_before, quantity_after, last_updated, product_name

)

SELECT

GETDATE(),

'UPDATE',

i.id,

i.product_id,

d.quantity,

i.quantity,

i.last_updated,

p.name

FROM inserted i

INNER JOIN deleted d ON i.id = d.id

LEFT JOIN store_product p ON i.product_id = p.id;

END;

\--FOR ORDERS:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_audit_store_order

ON store_order

AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

AS

BEGIN

SET NOCOUNT ON;

\-- Insert

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, customer_id, total, date_ordered)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'INSERT', i.id, i.customer_id, i.total, i.date_ordered FROM inserted i;

\-- Delete

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, customer_id, total, date_ordered)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'DELETE', d.id, d.customer_id, d.total, d.date_ordered FROM deleted d;

\-- Update

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, customer_id, total, date_ordered)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'UPDATE', i.id, i.customer_id, i.total, i.date_ordered FROM inserted i

INNER JOIN deleted d ON i.id = d.id;

END;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_audit_store_orderitem

ON store_orderitem

AFTER INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

AS

BEGIN

SET NOCOUNT ON;

\-- Insert

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, orderitem_id, product_id, quantity)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'INSERT', i.order_id, i.id, i.product_id, i.quantity FROM inserted i;

\-- Delete

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, orderitem_id, product_id, quantity)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'DELETE', d.order_id, d.id, d.product_id, d.quantity FROM deleted d;

\-- Update

INSERT INTO order_audit (action_time, action_type, order_id, orderitem_id, product_id, quantity)

SELECT GETDATE(), 'UPDATE', i.order_id, i.id, i.product_id, i.quantity FROM inserted i

INNER JOIN deleted d ON i.id = d.id;

END;

# Conclusion

SoleMates sets a new standard for online shoe shopping by blending **fashion and functionality**. With real-time stock updates, smooth user interactions, and a powerful database backbone, it delivers a seamless shopping experience that makes every click feel like a confident step forward. This project transformed a simple prototype into a **full-fledged e-commerce platform**, ready to stride into the future.
